# vitadeck-144: Let Deck Apps call linked computers through plugins

PR #144, closes #109, #110, #111 and includes #145. A 110-file feature in C, TypeScript, and docs, with a long PR body. This case measures what a review misses when it describes changed files it did not read.
- Title: the PR title, or its goal in plain words.
- Why: present. The PR body says "A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it."
- Size: very-large. Large is also fine: 110 files and about 7,400 changed lines, with 643 of them a deleted server that moved.
- Parts: zero to eight. One story is fine, and so are parts for the SDK, the companion, the listener, and the plugin tooling.
- Groups: about 12 to 20. The range in `case.json` is wide because past runs gave 7 to 26, all defensible on a change this size.
3. LAN Listener, which replaces the upload server: `src/net/`, `src/upload/`, `src/platform/lan_address*`, `tests/upload_*`.
4. Link store and JS getter: `src/host_control/`, `src/jslib/host_control.c`, `tests/host_control_link_harness.c`, with `src/core/json.*` and `src/core/util.*`, which it needs.
7. SDK CLI plugin build and scaffolds: `js/packages/sdk/cli/`.
- Turning off **Upload and link** lasts only until the next launch, because `toggle_listener` stores nothing and `main.c` calls `shell_start_listener` on every start.
- `lan_listener_start` reads the address once and `lan_address_detect` falls back to `127.0.0.1`, so the Shell can show a loopback address until the listener restarts.

- A failed Deck App Storage replace now says `Could not write Deck App Storage.`, and the old `Could not replace Deck App Storage.` text is gone, because `deck_app_storage.c` now calls `vd_replace_file`.
- `vd_replace_file` and `vd_read_replaced_file` in `src/core/util.c` are the temp and backup file replace moved from `deck_app_storage.c`, and the link store in `link.c` now uses them too.
- `withPublishedVersions` in `copy-templates.ts` rewrites workspace versions in every template `package.json`, not only the scaffold's.
- Cross on the Host Control screen forgets the focused computer at once, with no confirm step.
- `bootstrap.c` fails boot with `Could not initialize Host Control Links.` when `host_control_links_init` returns false.
- `linkVita` first asks the running companion for `capabilities` on loopback and refuses when none answers.
- The lines removed from `package_manifest.c` are `skip_json_value`, moved to `json.c` as `json_skip_value` with the same body.
- `createEventLog` drops the oldest event past 100 per plugin, and `wait` returns no sign of the gap, so a slow watcher loses events with no signal.
- `cpuPercent` keeps one module-level `previous` sample, so two Vitas each read the CPU share since the other's read.
- `config.vitas` stores the Vita's IP from `route`, and `isAllowed` compares the peer to that list, so a linked Vita that gets a new address receives 403.
- `lan_address_detect` on POSIX takes the first IPv4 interface that does not start with `127.`, so a host with a VPN or container network can show the wrong address.
- A document `lookFor` bullet says the PR body claims only read-only built-ins exist, while `core.notify` emits an event that any Deck App can watch.
- Do not write a file note that says a file or hunk was not fetched, not read, or unverified, or that gives only a line count such as "Adds 71 lines".
- Do not say `util.c` adds string or parsing helpers, or that `deck_app_storage.c` drops parsing helpers; the moved code replaces files.
- Do not say `bootstrap.c` starts the listener or that `main.c` starts the link store; `bootstrap.c` calls `host_control_links_init`, and `main.c` calls `shell_start_listener`.
- Do not say that turning off **Upload and link** persists across launches.
- Do not describe the removal in `package_manifest.c` as a change in manifest parsing; the helper moved with no change in behavior.
- Do not repeat the PR claim that only read-only built-ins exist as a fact; `core.notify` is a built-in that emits an event.

- Why this case exists: the skill used to allow eight fetches on a change past six files. Seven reviews written under that cap (Haiku medium and high, Sonnet low and high, Opus low and high, Grok low, skill 0.13.2) stated each `Must` at most three times, and most once or never. A file with no fetch got a note like "Host implementation." or "One added line; hunk not fetched."

- Blind grades with this list, one run each: Opus 5.5 high went from `must` 2/6 to 6/6 after the cap was removed, and Haiku 5.5 high from 1/6 to 3/6. The `Must` items came from what capped runs missed, so read the gain together with the false claims a grader finds, which this list did not choose.

- The eval grader on Opus 5.5 high, one run each: `must` 2/6 under the cap and 5/6 after it. A `sources FAIL` on these runs only means the review cited a source that is not frozen here, because they fetched sources live.

- Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, two trials each with the eval grader: `must` stayed at 1/6 or 2/6 after the cap went, while false bullets fell from 14 of 242 to 4 of 243 and files read rose from 8 to all 109. Its file notes average under seven words, so facts it read stay out of the review. A case line near 2/6 on this model does not mean the producer read too little.

- Each `Must not` about a file note comes from one of those reviews. Sonnet low swapped `main.c` and `bootstrap.c`. Grok low called the file replace helpers string and parsing helpers. Opus high wrote 21 notes that said "not fetched".

- Each `Must` sits in a file that no PR text describes and whose digest line gives only symbols or a line count. A review states it only when it read the hunk. The PR body and `#109` to `#111` state the other design facts, which is why those are not here.
- The `Good` list holds facts that need a second file or a trace across files, per `eval/review-criteria.md`.
- `Must` and `Must not` scores do not change the exit code. Read the case line, for example `must 1/6  mustNot 2/6`, and compare it with a run of the older skill.

- `together` holds file pairs that every past run kept in one group. `apart` holds layers that every past run split. There is no `mechanicalPaths` expect, because past runs did not agree on where the lockfile goes.

"title": "[Claude] Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI",

"body": "Slice B of `docs/adr/0004-host-control-sliced-delivery.md`. Depends on slice A (#109); parallel with slice C (#111). **Size: M.** Tier: `fast`. Choices below are decisions you can overturn.

## Package and CLI

`js/packages/host-companion` is a private package (unpublished in v1) for Node 22+. It runs from source with tsx as `pnpm --dir js host-companion <command>` and imports the slice A registry and types.

- **`start`** binds `0.0.0.0:8797` and serves `POST /command`. The port is configurable but never falls forward like Runtime Upload's, because the Vita stores the URL and a moved port would break the link silently. A busy port exits non-zero.
- **`link <vita-address>`** first checks that `start` answers `capabilities` on loopback, so a link never points at nothing. It then POSTs the slice A link payload, prints the result and exits.

**Pairing decision.** The user reads the Vita's address on the Shell Host Control Screen and passes it to `link`, which is the ADR's topology C. I rejected a companion-shown code: the Vita would have to find the computer, by mDNS (new native work) or by typing on the Vita (rejected topology A), and a code is a credential, which the ADR defers.

**Advertised URL.** `link` connects a UDP socket to the Vita's IP and reads `address()`. That yields the interface the OS routes to the Vita, never VPN or Docker; `--advertise <ip>` overrides it.

## Serving

```ts
const implementations = {
  capabilities: async () => ({
    protocolVersion: HOST_CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
    name: os.hostname(),
    platform: process.platform,
    commands: enabledCommands(),
  }),
  echo: async ({ text }) => ({ text }),
} satisfies HostCommandImplementations; // mapped over slice A's registry
```

A missing or mistyped implementation fails `tsc`. Requests are checked in order (route, method, content type, size, protocol version, command, payload guard), and each check fails with a slice A code.

**Peer check.** Once linked, `/command` answers only the linked Vita's IP and this computer's own addresses, so the desktop host build still works. Every other peer gets `forbidden`. IPs can be spoofed, so this is no credential, but it narrows "any LAN peer" to one device.

## Config, logs, background

- **Config.** `~/.vitadeck/host-companion.json` holds `{ "port": 8797, "advertise": null, "vita": "192.168.1.177", "enable": [] }`. `link` writes `vita`.
- **Logs.** One stdout line per request (time, peer, command, code, ms), never payloads.
- **Background.** The OS handles this in v1. The README gives a macOS launchd agent, a Windows "at log on" scheduled task, and the firewall prompt to accept. There is no tray icon or installer.

## Computer-acting commands

None here. After the credential decision, each gets its own PR, off by default: served and listed in `capabilities` only when `enable` names it. First candidates: `mediaPlayPause`, `launchApp`.

## Tests

`node --test`, in the `fast` tier:

- slice A's fixtures replayed against `start` on port 0
- a stub Vita (`node:http` serving `POST /link`), checking that `link` handles ok, a version mismatch and an unreachable Vita
- slice A's `createHostClient` against the real server
- the peer check, using an injected remote address

**Files:** new `js/packages/host-companion/` (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `README.md`, `src/{cli,server,link,config,commands}.ts` and tests), plus `js/package.json` and `scripts/agent-check.sh`.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-opus-5-5]

"title": "[Claude] Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen",

"body": "Slice C of `docs/adr/0004-host-control-sliced-delivery.md`. Depends on slice A (#109) for the payload, fixtures and getter name; parallel with slice B (#110). **Size: L.** Tier: `full`. Choices are decisions you can overturn.

## Shell

- **Shell Host Control Entry:** a new row after the Shell Upload Entry, captioned `Linked: <name>` or `Not linked`. Confirm opens the screen.
- **Shell Host Control Screen** (`VD_SHELL_HOST_CONTROL`): entering it starts the listener. It shows `Link address: 192.168.1.177:8798`, a hint to give it to the Host Companion's `link`, and a status line (waiting, bind error, or `Linked to <name> at <url>`). Cross on `Forget link` clears the link with no confirm step, since relinking is cheap.
- **Listener lifetime**, per the ADR: it stops when a link succeeds, on Circle (back to Home), on Start (Shell hides), and on exit (`shell_shutdown`). Runtime Upload is untouched, and both listeners can run at once.
- **Input:** no new keys, and `src/ui/input.c` is unchanged. In `CONTEXT.md`, **Shell Face Input** gains "Circle leaves the Host Control screen".

## Shared HTTP parsing

- No picohttpparser. `src/upload/http_parse.*` moves into `src/net/http.{c,h}`, together with `read_request`, `send_response`, `send_json_error` and the drain helpers from `http_server.c`. Upload behaves exactly as before.
- LAN address detection moves into `src/platform/`: `lan_address_posix.c` uses `getifaddrs` and `lan_address_vita.c` uses `sceNetCtl`.
- The ADR's case-sensitive header defect is already fixed on `main` (`strncasecmp`, covered by `upload_parsing_harness`). Rewrite that ADR sentence in place.

## Listener, store, getter

- **`src/host_control/listener.c`** binds 8798. It falls forward up to 10 ports (safe, since the address is on screen) and stays clear of upload (8787–8796) and the companion (8797) on one Mac. One accept thread handles connections inline with a 2 s receive timeout, and the only route is `POST /link`. The Shell polls it the way it polls upload.
- **`src/host_control/link.c`** holds `host_control_link_parse`, a pure jimp parser. It accepts `protocolVersion == 1`, an `http://` `url` of at most 255 bytes with no spaces or control bytes, and a `name` of 1 to 64 bytes. It also keeps the mutex-guarded current link in `<data root>/host-control-link.json`, saved with `deck_app_storage`'s Vita-safe replace. The newest link wins, and forgetting deletes the file.
- **`src/jslib/host_control.c`** registers `nativeGetHostControlUrl(): string` (`""` when unlinked) and declares it in `runtime-native.d.ts`. Reads are live, so a running Deck App's next command uses the new link.

## Vita vs host

Sockets, `vd_thread` and `package_library_data_root()` already cover both; the LAN address is the only new platform code. `full` proves the Vita build; ask Máté before hardware testing.

## Tests

`tests/host_control_link_harness.c` (CTest):

- Slice A's `link-*.json` fixtures run through the parser.
- Store round trip: save, reload, forget.
- Loopback: start the listener, POST a fixture with lowercase headers, and assert the reply, the stored URL, and that the listener stopped.

Upload harnesses keep passing; one manual host-window pass, with screenshots in the PR.

**Docs:** `CONTEXT.md` (both Shell terms above, **Host Control Link Listener**, Shell Home Screen), the ADR sentence, and `AGENTS.md` "Where code lives".

**Files:** `src/net/`, `src/upload/http_server.c`, `src/platform/lan_address*`, `src/host_control/`, `src/jslib/{host_control,jslib}.c`, `src/shell/shell.{c,h}`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/host_control_link_harness.c`, `js/packages/runtime/src/runtime-native.d.ts`.

"title": "feat(host-control): Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as a .vdplugin package",

"body": "Follow-up to #144, stacked on its branch. From an external author's or user's side, Host Control Plugins were clunky:
- a custom plugin meant an npm package of its own;
- a globally installed companion couldn't load a plugin installed somewhere else;
- the CLI was only `pnpm --dir js host-companion`.

The compromise is built-in plugins first, plus a package, like the Deck App's, for each Deck App's own plugin:

- **Built-ins.** Every companion now has `core` and `systemStats`. Deck Apps import the definitions from `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`, together with `implementHostPlugin` and `HostCommandError`. `js/host-plugins/` is gone. Keys, media and opening apps are the next built-ins, but each one acts on the computer, so they wait for the credentials decision (ADR 0004).
- **A custom plugin lives in the Deck App's repo.**
  - `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin` scaffolds `host/plugin.ts` (the commands) and `host/companion.ts` (the implementation).
  - `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `vitadeck build` and `vitadeck dev` also write a `dist/my-app.vdplugin/` package and a `dist/my-app.vdplugin.zip` archive. The package holds `manifest.json`, `companion.mjs` (the implementation with its npm dependencies bundled in) and an optional `files/` folder.
  - It's a package rather than one file because plugins will carry more than code: scripts, data, binaries. The entry reads them through `import.meta.url`.
- **Users install the archive:** `vitadeck-host-companion install my-app.vdplugin.zip` / `remove my-app`. A running companion reloads its plugins folder and any `--plugin` package or folder when they change, so the author's loop is `pnpm host` (`--plugin ./dist`) plus `vitadeck dev`, with no restarts.
- **Two CLIs, one per machine role.** `vitadeck` builds Deck Apps and plugin files; `vitadeck-host-companion` runs on any computer a Vita controls.
  - I didn't fold the companion into `vitadeck host`: a second command in the SDK package would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk`, and users shouldn't need Babel and rolldown just to run a server.
  - The companion is bundled into a single file with no dependencies. It stays `private: true` until a release.
  - The Shell's link hint now names `vitadeck-host-companion`.

ADR 0004, CONTEXT.md (new term: **Host Plugin Package**), AGENTS.md and the SDK, companion and demo READMEs are updated in place.

## Proof

- `scripts/agent-check.sh full` passed on 148fceef: JS checks, CTest, Docker smoke and the Vita VPK. Later commits change only JS: review fixes and the package format. On the head, `tsc`, lint, SDK tests (36) and companion tests (30) pass, and CI runs build, smoke and the Vita build.
- New tests:
  - `create --host-plugin` gives a project that passes `tsc` for both the app and `host/`, builds the package and zip with a self-contained entry, and whose `greet` command runs.
  - `hostPlugin.files` lands in `files/`, and a missing entry fails the build.
  - A package's entry reads its own `files/` through `import.meta.url`.
  - The companion CLI end to end: `install` of a `.vdplugin.zip` loads into a running companion, and `remove` unloads it. In a `--plugin ./dist` folder, a rebuilt package reloads and a broken rebuild keeps the previous one. `install` refuses built-in ids and anything but an archive or package.
  - Malformed manifests, entries outside the package, and zips with several roots or `../` paths are refused.
  - A bundled CommonJS dependency loads, because the entry is imported by file URL.
- I ran it as an external user in the macOS host window: [screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-plugin-screenshots/).
  - I packed both packages, installed the companion globally into a temp prefix (it adds one package), and scaffolded `lights` outside the repo.
  - Install of the `.vdplugin.zip`, link and Greet worked, with Greet's reply including text the plugin read from its packaged `files/motd.txt`.
  - Editing the plugin and rebuilding changed the answer live; after `remove`, the app showed `unknown_plugin`.

## How to test

Run these from the repo root on the host build; they use your real `~/.vitadeck/`.

1. Set up:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js install && cmake --preset default && ninja -C out run
   ```
2. In a second terminal, pack both packages and act as an external user:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js build && mkdir -p /tmp/vdp
   pnpm --dir js --filter @vitadeck/sdk --filter @vitadeck/host-companion pack --pack-destination /tmp/vdp
   npm i -g --prefix /tmp/vdp/global /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz
   export PATH=/tmp/vdp/global/bin:$PATH
   cd /tmp/vdp && vitadeck create lights --host-plugin && cd lights
   npm pkg set "dependencies.@vitadeck/sdk=file:../vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz" "devDependencies.@vitadeck/host-companion=file:../vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz"
   npm install && npm run tsc && npm run host
   ```
   The `npm pkg set` line only stands in for npm publishing.
3. In VitaDeck, press F1 and confirm **Upload**. In a third terminal (same `PATH`), from `/tmp/vdp/lights`, run `npx vitadeck dev <upload URL>`.
4. In VitaDeck, open **Host Control** and run `vitadeck-host-companion link <address>`.
5. Press F1, run **lights**, then press Enter on **Greet**.
6. Edit the message in `host/companion.ts` and save. `vitadeck dev` rebuilds, the companion prints `Reloaded plugins`, and Greet shows the new text.
7. To try the user path:
   1. Stop `npm run host`, then run `vitadeck-host-companion install dist/lights.vdplugin.zip && vitadeck-host-companion start`. Greet still works.
   2. Run `vitadeck-host-companion remove lights`. Greet shows `unknown_plugin`.

"body": "A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it. This adds **Host Control**: link a computer once, and Deck Apps can call typed commands on it over the LAN. Commands come in plugins: built-ins every computer has, and custom ones an author writes, either with a Deck App or on their own. Plugins can also push events to Deck Apps the moment something happens on the computer. Closes #109, #110, #111; includes #145.

The design leaves room for later use cases without changing the contract: keyboard shortcuts, sensor gauges with controls, a Stream Deck-style grid, one Deck App driving several machines on different OSes, and a T3 Code dashboard. None of those are built here.

## How it works

- **Link once, then the Vita calls the companion** (ADR 0004, topology C).
  - VitaDeck starts one **LAN Listener** at boot (port 8787) for both Runtime Upload and links. The Shell's **Upload and link** row shows its URL and turns it off and on.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion link <vita-ip>` sends it the companion's id, name and URL; `vitadeck dev <vita-ip>` uses the same address. Nothing needs opening in the Shell first.
  - VitaDeck keeps up to 4 links, newest first, one per companion id.
  - Every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked (`relink: true`), so a new computer IP or port reaches them without `link`. VitaDeck updates only a link it still has; a computer forgotten in the Shell gets 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita that is off is retried every 30 s.
- **SDK:** `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` is an additive subpath. `createHostClient(plugin, { hostId })` and `linkedHosts()` support several machines. Calls resolve to `{ ok: true, ...result }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }` and never reject.
- **Plugins:** a plugin is a typed registry (`defineHostPlugin(id, { name: command<Payload, Result>(guard) })`) that Deck Apps import, plus an implementation (`implementHostPlugin`) that the companion runs. TypeScript fails a missing or mistyped implementation, and the companion checks every payload.
  - **Built-in:** `core` (`capabilities`, `echo`, `events`, `notify`) and `systemStats` (CPU, memory, uptime) ship in every companion. Their registries come from the SDK.
  - **Custom:** `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json`. `vitadeck build` writes a `<slug>.vdplugin/` package (`manifest.json`, bundled `companion.mjs`, optional `files/`) and a `<slug>.vdplugin.zip`, like a Deck App's `.vdapp`.
    - With a Deck App: `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin`.
    - Standalone: `vitadeck create lights --host-plugin-only` makes a project with no `entry`. Its `package.json` exports the registry, so any Deck App can depend on it (local path, git, or npm), with `@vitadeck/sdk` as a peer dependency.
- **Host Companion** (`@vitadeck/host-companion`, bin `vitadeck-host-companion`): one dependency-free bundle that stays `private` until a release.
  - `start`, `link`, `install <x.vdplugin.zip>`, `remove <id>`.
  - Installed plugins live in `~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin`.
  - A running companion reloads them and any `--plugin ./dist` folder when they change, so an author's loop is `pnpm host` plus `vitadeck dev`.
  - `vitadeck` builds and `vitadeck-host-companion` runs. A single CLI would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk` and make users install the build toolchain just to run a server.
- **Events (computer → Vita), by long-polling:**
  - Plugins declare typed events (`defineHostPlugin(id, commands, { changed: event<Data>() })`) and emit them from a `start(emit)` lifecycle, which the companion runs while the plugin is loaded.
  - `core.events({ plugin, after })` answers at once, or holds the request until that plugin's next event, up to 25 s. The companion keeps 100 events per plugin.
  - `watchHostEvents(plugin, onEvent, { hostId })` keeps one wait open, so events arrive within a round trip and none fall between two waits.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion notify "Build done"` sends a `core` notice that any Deck App can watch; the demo shows it.
  - Native `fetch` now cancels pending requests when a Deck App stops, so a held wait never stalls a reload. WebSocket, SSE and a Vita listener were considered and rejected in ADR 0004.
- **Native:**
  - The upload server becomes the LAN Listener (`src/net/lan_listener.c`) with a `POST /link` route, and its request parsing moves to `src/net/http.c`.
  - `src/host_control/` adds the link store, `src/platform/lan_address_*` the shown address, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` exposes links to JS.
  - The Shell gains the **Upload and link** toggle (Runtime Upload used to start only from the Shell) and a Host Control screen that shows the `link` command and lists and forgets linked computers.
  - Because the listener now runs from boot, anyone on the LAN can upload a Deck App or add a link whenever VitaDeck runs, until credentials exist (ADR 0004).
- **Demo:** `js/examples/host-control` lists every linked computer with live CPU, and for the selected one shows its capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip.

+# vitadeck-144: Let Deck Apps call linked computers through plugins
+
+PR #144, closes #109, #110, #111 and includes #145. A 110-file feature in C, TypeScript, and docs, with a long PR body. This case measures what a review misses when it describes changed files it did not read.
+
+## Story
+
+- Title: the PR title, or its goal in plain words.
+- Why: present. The PR body says "A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it."
+- Size: very-large. Large is also fine: 110 files and about 7,400 changed lines, with 643 of them a deleted server that moved.
+- Parts: zero to eight. One story is fine, and so are parts for the SDK, the companion, the listener, and the plugin tooling.
+- Groups: about 12 to 20. The range in `case.json` is wide because past runs gave 7 to 26, all defensible on a change this size.
+
+## Groups
+
+1. SDK wire contract and client: `js/packages/sdk/src/host-control/`, `js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.ts`, `tests/fixtures/host-control/`.
+2. Host Companion: `js/packages/host-companion/`.
+3. LAN Listener, which replaces the upload server: `src/net/`, `src/upload/`, `src/platform/lan_address*`, `tests/upload_*`.
+4. Link store and JS getter: `src/host_control/`, `src/jslib/host_control.c`, `tests/host_control_link_harness.c`, with `src/core/json.*` and `src/core/util.*`, which it needs.
+5. Shell: `src/shell/`, `tests/shell_input_harness.c`, `src/main.c`, `src/core/bootstrap.c`.
+6. Native fetch cancel: `src/jslib/fetch.c`, `tests/js_limits_harness.c`.
+7. SDK CLI plugin build and scaffolds: `js/packages/sdk/cli/`.
+8. Demo, docs, and tooling: `js/examples/host-control/`, `docs/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `.agents/skills/`, `scripts/agent-check.sh`.
+
+## Must
+
+- Turning off **Upload and link** lasts only until the next launch, because `toggle_listener` stores nothing and `main.c` calls `shell_start_listener` on every start.
+- `lan_listener_start` reads the address once and `lan_address_detect` falls back to `127.0.0.1`, so the Shell can show a loopback address until the listener restarts.
+- A failed Deck App Storage replace now says `Could not write Deck App Storage.`, and the old `Could not replace Deck App Storage.` text is gone, because `deck_app_storage.c` now calls `vd_replace_file`.
+- `vd_replace_file` and `vd_read_replaced_file` in `src/core/util.c` are the temp and backup file replace moved from `deck_app_storage.c`, and the link store in `link.c` now uses them too.
+- `withPublishedVersions` in `copy-templates.ts` rewrites workspace versions in every template `package.json`, not only the scaffold's.
+- Cross on the Host Control screen forgets the focused computer at once, with no confirm step.
+
+## Good
+
+- `bootstrap.c` fails boot with `Could not initialize Host Control Links.` when `host_control_links_init` returns false.
+- `linkVita` first asks the running companion for `capabilities` on loopback and refuses when none answers.
+- The lines removed from `package_manifest.c` are `skip_json_value`, moved to `json.c` as `json_skip_value` with the same body.
+- `createEventLog` drops the oldest event past 100 per plugin, and `wait` returns no sign of the gap, so a slow watcher loses events with no signal.
+- `cpuPercent` keeps one module-level `previous` sample, so two Vitas each read the CPU share since the other's read.
+- `config.vitas` stores the Vita's IP from `route`, and `isAllowed` compares the peer to that list, so a linked Vita that gets a new address receives 403.
+- `lan_address_detect` on POSIX takes the first IPv4 interface that does not start with `127.`, so a host with a VPN or container network can show the wrong address.
+- A document `lookFor` bullet says the PR body claims only read-only built-ins exist, while `core.notify` emits an event that any Deck App can watch.
+
+## Must not
+
+- Do not write a file note that says a file or hunk was not fetched, not read, or unverified, or that gives only a line count such as "Adds 71 lines".
+- Do not say `util.c` adds string or parsing helpers, or that `deck_app_storage.c` drops parsing helpers; the moved code replaces files.
+- Do not say `bootstrap.c` starts the listener or that `main.c` starts the link store; `bootstrap.c` calls `host_control_links_init`, and `main.c` calls `shell_start_listener`.
+- Do not say that turning off **Upload and link** persists across launches.
+- Do not describe the removal in `package_manifest.c` as a change in manifest parsing; the helper moved with no change in behavior.
+- Do not repeat the PR claim that only read-only built-ins exist as a fact; `core.notify` is a built-in that emits an event.
+
+## Notes
+
+- Why this case exists: the skill used to allow eight fetches on a change past six files. Seven reviews written under that cap (Haiku medium and high, Sonnet low and high, Opus low and high, Grok low, skill 0.13.2) stated each `Must` at most three times, and most once or never. A file with no fetch got a note like "Host implementation." or "One added line; hunk not fetched."
+- Blind grades with this list, one run each: Opus 5.5 high went from `must` 2/6 to 6/6 after the cap was removed, and Haiku 5.5 high from 1/6 to 3/6. The `Must` items came from what capped runs missed, so read the gain together with the false claims a grader finds, which this list did not choose.
+- The eval grader on Opus 5.5 high, one run each: `must` 2/6 under the cap and 5/6 after it. A `sources FAIL` on these runs only means the review cited a source that is not frozen here, because they fetched sources live.
+- Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, two trials each with the eval grader: `must` stayed at 1/6 or 2/6 after the cap went, while false bullets fell from 14 of 242 to 4 of 243 and files read rose from 8 to all 109. Its file notes average under seven words, so facts it read stay out of the review. A case line near 2/6 on this model does not mean the producer read too little.
+- Each `Must not` about a file note comes from one of those reviews. Sonnet low swapped `main.c` and `bootstrap.c`. Grok low called the file replace helpers string and parsing helpers. Opus high wrote 21 notes that said "not fetched".
+- Each `Must` sits in a file that no PR text describes and whose digest line gives only symbols or a line count. A review states it only when it read the hunk. The PR body and `#109` to `#111` state the other design facts, which is why those are not here.
+- The `Good` list holds facts that need a second file or a trace across files, per `eval/review-criteria.md`.
+- `Must` and `Must not` scores do not change the exit code. Read the case line, for example `must 1/6  mustNot 2/6`, and compare it with a run of the older skill.
+- `together` holds file pairs that every past run kept in one group. `apart` holds layers that every past run split. There is no `mechanicalPaths` expect, because past runs did not agree on where the lockfile goes.

## Package and CLI

`js/packages/host-companion` is a private package (unpublished in v1) for Node 22+. It runs from source with tsx as `pnpm --dir js host-companion <command>` and imports the slice A registry and types.

- **`start`** binds `0.0.0.0:8797` and serves `POST /command`. The port is configurable but never falls forward like Runtime Upload's, because the Vita stores the URL and a moved port would break the link silently. A busy port exits non-zero.
- **`link <vita-address>`** first checks that `start` answers `capabilities` on loopback, so a link never points at nothing. It then POSTs the slice A link payload, prints the result and exits.

**Pairing decision.** The user reads the Vita's address on the Shell Host Control Screen and passes it to `link`, which is the ADR's topology C. I rejected a companion-shown code: the Vita would have to find the computer, by mDNS (new native work) or by typing on the Vita (rejected topology A), and a code is a credential, which the ADR defers.

**Advertised URL.** `link` connects a UDP socket to the Vita's IP and reads `address()`. That yields the interface the OS routes to the Vita, never VPN or Docker; `--advertise <ip>` overrides it.

## Serving

```ts
const implementations = {
  capabilities: async () => ({
    protocolVersion: HOST_CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
    name: os.hostname(),
    platform: process.platform,
    commands: enabledCommands(),
  }),
  echo: async ({ text }) => ({ text }),
} satisfies HostCommandImplementations; // mapped over slice A's registry
```

A missing or mistyped implementation fails `tsc`. Requests are checked in order (route, method, content type, size, protocol version, command, payload guard), and each check fails with a slice A code.

**Peer check.** Once linked, `/command` answers only the linked Vita's IP and this computer's own addresses, so the desktop host build still works. Every other peer gets `forbidden`. IPs can be spoofed, so this is no credential, but it narrows "any LAN peer" to one device.

- **Config.** `~/.vitadeck/host-companion.json` holds `{ "port": 8797, "advertise": null, "vita": "192.168.1.177", "enable": [] }`. `link` writes `vita`.
- **Logs.** One stdout line per request (time, peer, command, code, ms), never payloads.
- **Background.** The OS handles this in v1. The README gives a macOS launchd agent, a Windows "at log on" scheduled task, and the firewall prompt to accept. There is no tray icon or installer.

## Computer-acting commands

None here. After the credential decision, each gets its own PR, off by default: served and listed in `capabilities` only when `enable` names it. First candidates: `mediaPlayPause`, `launchApp`.

`node --test`, in the `fast` tier:

- slice A's fixtures replayed against `start` on port 0
- a stub Vita (`node:http` serving `POST /link`), checking that `link` handles ok, a version mismatch and an unreachable Vita
- slice A's `createHostClient` against the real server
- the peer check, using an injected remote address

**Files:** new `js/packages/host-companion/` (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `README.md`, `src/{cli,server,link,config,commands}.ts` and tests), plus `js/package.json` and `scripts/agent-check.sh`.

+  "body": "Slice C of `docs/adr/0004-host-control-sliced-delivery.md`. Depends on slice A (#109) for the payload, fixtures and getter name; parallel with slice B (#110). **Size: L.** Tier: `full`. Choices are decisions you can overturn.

## Shell

- **Shell Host Control Entry:** a new row after the Shell Upload Entry, captioned `Linked: <name>` or `Not linked`. Confirm opens the screen.
- **Shell Host Control Screen** (`VD_SHELL_HOST_CONTROL`): entering it starts the listener. It shows `Link address: 192.168.1.177:8798`, a hint to give it to the Host Companion's `link`, and a status line (waiting, bind error, or `Linked to <name> at <url>`). Cross on `Forget link` clears the link with no confirm step, since relinking is cheap.
- **Listener lifetime**, per the ADR: it stops when a link succeeds, on Circle (back to Home), on Start (Shell hides), and on exit (`shell_shutdown`). Runtime Upload is untouched, and both listeners can run at once.
- **Input:** no new keys, and `src/ui/input.c` is unchanged. In `CONTEXT.md`, **Shell Face Input** gains "Circle leaves the Host Control screen".

## Shared HTTP parsing

- No picohttpparser. `src/upload/http_parse.*` moves into `src/net/http.{c,h}`, together with `read_request`, `send_response`, `send_json_error` and the drain helpers from `http_server.c`. Upload behaves exactly as before.
- LAN address detection moves into `src/platform/`: `lan_address_posix.c` uses `getifaddrs` and `lan_address_vita.c` uses `sceNetCtl`.
- The ADR's case-sensitive header defect is already fixed on `main` (`strncasecmp`, covered by `upload_parsing_harness`). Rewrite that ADR sentence in place.

## Listener, store, getter

- **`src/host_control/listener.c`** binds 8798. It falls forward up to 10 ports (safe, since the address is on screen) and stays clear of upload (8787–8796) and the companion (8797) on one Mac. One accept thread handles connections inline with a 2 s receive timeout, and the only route is `POST /link`. The Shell polls it the way it polls upload.
- **`src/host_control/link.c`** holds `host_control_link_parse`, a pure jimp parser. It accepts `protocolVersion == 1`, an `http://` `url` of at most 255 bytes with no spaces or control bytes, and a `name` of 1 to 64 bytes. It also keeps the mutex-guarded current link in `<data root>/host-control-link.json`, saved with `deck_app_storage`'s Vita-safe replace. The newest link wins, and forgetting deletes the file.
- **`src/jslib/host_control.c`** registers `nativeGetHostControlUrl(): string` (`""` when unlinked) and declares it in `runtime-native.d.ts`. Reads are live, so a running Deck App's next command uses the new link.

## Vita vs host

Sockets, `vd_thread` and `package_library_data_root()` already cover both; the LAN address is the only new platform code. `full` proves the Vita build; ask Máté before hardware testing.

`tests/host_control_link_harness.c` (CTest):

- Slice A's `link-*.json` fixtures run through the parser.
- Store round trip: save, reload, forget.
- Loopback: start the listener, POST a fixture with lowercase headers, and assert the reply, the stored URL, and that the listener stopped.

Upload harnesses keep passing; one manual host-window pass, with screenshots in the PR.

+{
+  "html_url": "https://github.com/matemolnar8/vitadeck/pull/145",
+  "number": 145,
+  "title": "feat(host-control): Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as a .vdplugin package",
+  "body": "Follow-up to #144, stacked on its branch. From an external author's or user's side, Host Control Plugins were clunky:
- a custom plugin meant an npm package of its own;
- a globally installed companion couldn't load a plugin installed somewhere else;
- the CLI was only `pnpm --dir js host-companion`.

The compromise is built-in plugins first, plus a package, like the Deck App's, for each Deck App's own plugin:

- **Built-ins.** Every companion now has `core` and `systemStats`. Deck Apps import the definitions from `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`, together with `implementHostPlugin` and `HostCommandError`. `js/host-plugins/` is gone. Keys, media and opening apps are the next built-ins, but each one acts on the computer, so they wait for the credentials decision (ADR 0004).
- **A custom plugin lives in the Deck App's repo.**
  - `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin` scaffolds `host/plugin.ts` (the commands) and `host/companion.ts` (the implementation).
  - `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `vitadeck build` and `vitadeck dev` also write a `dist/my-app.vdplugin/` package and a `dist/my-app.vdplugin.zip` archive. The package holds `manifest.json`, `companion.mjs` (the implementation with its npm dependencies bundled in) and an optional `files/` folder.
  - It's a package rather than one file because plugins will carry more than code: scripts, data, binaries. The entry reads them through `import.meta.url`.
- **Users install the archive:** `vitadeck-host-companion install my-app.vdplugin.zip` / `remove my-app`. A running companion reloads its plugins folder and any `--plugin` package or folder when they change, so the author's loop is `pnpm host` (`--plugin ./dist`) plus `vitadeck dev`, with no restarts.
- **Two CLIs, one per machine role.** `vitadeck` builds Deck Apps and plugin files; `vitadeck-host-companion` runs on any computer a Vita controls.
  - I didn't fold the companion into `vitadeck host`: a second command in the SDK package would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk`, and users shouldn't need Babel and rolldown just to run a server.
  - The companion is bundled into a single file with no dependencies. It stays `private: true` until a release.
  - The Shell's link hint now names `vitadeck-host-companion`.

ADR 0004, CONTEXT.md (new term: **Host Plugin Package**), AGENTS.md and the SDK, companion and demo READMEs are updated in place.

## Proof

- `scripts/agent-check.sh full` passed on 148fceef: JS checks, CTest, Docker smoke and the Vita VPK. Later commits change only JS: review fixes and the package format. On the head, `tsc`, lint, SDK tests (36) and companion tests (30) pass, and CI runs build, smoke and the Vita build.
- New tests:
  - `create --host-plugin` gives a project that passes `tsc` for both the app and `host/`, builds the package and zip with a self-contained entry, and whose `greet` command runs.
  - `hostPlugin.files` lands in `files/`, and a missing entry fails the build.
  - A package's entry reads its own `files/` through `import.meta.url`.
  - The companion CLI end to end: `install` of a `.vdplugin.zip` loads into a running companion, and `remove` unloads it. In a `--plugin ./dist` folder, a rebuilt package reloads and a broken rebuild keeps the previous one. `install` refuses built-in ids and anything but an archive or package.
  - Malformed manifests, entries outside the package, and zips with several roots or `../` paths are refused.
  - A bundled CommonJS dependency loads, because the entry is imported by file URL.
- I ran it as an external user in the macOS host window: [screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-plugin-screenshots/).
  - I packed both packages, installed the companion globally into a temp prefix (it adds one package), and scaffolded `lights` outside the repo.
  - Install of the `.vdplugin.zip`, link and Greet worked, with Greet's reply including text the plugin read from its packaged `files/motd.txt`.
  - Editing the plugin and rebuilding changed the answer live; after `remove`, the app showed `unknown_plugin`.

## How to test

Run these from the repo root on the host build; they use your real `~/.vitadeck/`.

1. Set up:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js install && cmake --preset default && ninja -C out run
   ```
2. In a second terminal, pack both packages and act as an external user:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js build && mkdir -p /tmp/vdp
   pnpm --dir js --filter @vitadeck/sdk --filter @vitadeck/host-companion pack --pack-destination /tmp/vdp
   npm i -g --prefix /tmp/vdp/global /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz
   export PATH=/tmp/vdp/global/bin:$PATH
   cd /tmp/vdp && vitadeck create lights --host-plugin && cd lights
   npm pkg set "dependencies.@vitadeck/sdk=file:../vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz" "devDependencies.@vitadeck/host-companion=file:../vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz"
   npm install && npm run tsc && npm run host
   ```
   The `npm pkg set` line only stands in for npm publishing.
3. In VitaDeck, press F1 and confirm **Upload**. In a third terminal (same `PATH`), from `/tmp/vdp/lights`, run `npx vitadeck dev <upload URL>`.
4. In VitaDeck, open **Host Control** and run `vitadeck-host-companion link <address>`.
5. Press F1, run **lights**, then press Enter on **Greet**.
6. Edit the message in `host/companion.ts` and save. `vitadeck dev` rebuilds, the companion prints `Reloaded plugins`, and Greet shows the new text.

- **Link once, then the Vita calls the companion** (ADR 0004, topology C).

  - VitaDeck keeps up to 4 links, newest first, one per companion id.
  - Every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked (`relink: true`), so a new computer IP or port reaches them without `link`. VitaDeck updates only a link it still has; a computer forgotten in the Shell gets 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita that is off is retried every 30 s.
- **SDK:** `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` is an additive subpath. `createHostClient(plugin, { hostId })` and `linkedHosts()` support several machines. Calls resolve to `{ ok: true, ...result }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }` and never reject.
- **Plugins:** a plugin is a typed registry (`defineHostPlugin(id, { name: command<Payload, Result>(guard) })`) that Deck Apps import, plus an implementation (`implementHostPlugin`) that the companion runs. lines.text: "title": "feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins",

"body": "A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it. This adds **Host Control**: link a computer once, and Deck Apps can call typed commands on it over the LAN. Commands come in plugins: built-ins every computer has, and custom ones an author writes, either with a Deck App or on their own. Plugins can also push events to Deck Apps the moment something happens on the computer. Closes #109, #110, #111; includes #145.

The design leaves room for later use cases without changing the contract: keyboard shortcuts, sensor gauges with controls, a Stream Deck-style grid, one Deck App driving several machines on different OSes, and a T3 Code dashboard. None of those are built here.

## How it works

- **Link once, then the Vita calls the companion** (ADR 0004, topology C).
  - VitaDeck starts one **LAN Listener** at boot (port 8787) for both Runtime Upload and links. The Shell's **Upload and link** row shows its URL and turns it off and on.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion link <vita-ip>` sends it the companion's id, name and URL; `vitadeck dev <vita-ip>` uses the same address. Nothing needs opening in the Shell first.
  - VitaDeck keeps up to 4 links, newest first, one per companion id.
  - Every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked (`relink: true`), so a new computer IP or port reaches them without `link`. VitaDeck updates only a link it still has; a computer forgotten in the Shell gets 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita that is off is retried every 30 s.
- **SDK:** `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` is an additive subpath. `createHostClient(plugin, { hostId })` and `linkedHosts()` support several machines. Calls resolve to `{ ok: true, ...result }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }` and never reject.
- **Plugins:** a plugin is a typed registry (`defineHostPlugin(id, { name: command<Payload, Result>(guard) })`) that Deck Apps import, plus an implementation (`implementHostPlugin`) that the companion runs. TypeScript fails a missing or mistyped implementation, and the companion checks every payload.
  - **Built-in:** `core` (`capabilities`, `echo`, `events`, `notify`) and `systemStats` (CPU, memory, uptime) ship in every companion. Their registries come from the SDK.
  - **Custom:** `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json`. `vitadeck build` writes a `<slug>.vdplugin/` package (`manifest.json`, bundled `companion.mjs`, optional `files/`) and a `<slug>.vdplugin.zip`, like a Deck App's `.vdapp`.
    - With a Deck App: `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin`.
    - Standalone: `vitadeck create lights --host-plugin-only` makes a project with no `entry`. Its `package.json` exports the registry, so any Deck App can depend on it (local path, git, or npm), with `@vitadeck/sdk` as a peer dependency.
- **Host Companion** (`@vitadeck/host-companion`, bin `vitadeck-host-companion`): one dependency-free bundle that stays `private` until a release.
  - `start`, `link`, `install <x.vdplugin.zip>`, `remove <id>`.
  - Installed plugins live in `~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin`.
  - A running companion reloads them and any `--plugin ./dist` folder when they change, so an author's loop is `pnpm host` plus `vitadeck dev`.
  - `vitadeck` builds and `vitadeck-host-companion` runs. A single CLI would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk` and make users install the build toolchain just to run a server.
- **Events (computer → Vita), by long-polling:**
  - Plugins declare typed events (`defineHostPlugin(id, commands, { changed: event<Data>() })`) and emit them from a `start(emit)` lifecycle, which the companion runs while the plugin is loaded.
  - `core.events({ plugin, after })` answers at once, or holds the request until that plugin's next event, up to 25 s. The companion keeps 100 events per plugin.
  - `watchHostEvents(plugin, onEvent, { hostId })` keeps one wait open, so events arrive within a round trip and none fall between two waits.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion notify "Build done"` sends a `core` notice that any Deck App can watch; the demo shows it.
  - Native `fetch` now cancels pending requests when a Deck App stops, so a held wait never stalls a reload. WebSocket, SSE and a Vita listener were considered and rejected in ADR 0004.
- **Native:**
  - The upload server becomes the LAN Listener (`src/net/lan_listener.c`) with a `POST /link` route, and its request parsing moves to `src/net/http.c`.
  - `src/host_control/` adds the link store, `src/platform/lan_address_*` the shown address, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` exposes links to JS.
  - The Shell gains the **Upload and link** toggle (Runtime Upload used to start only from the Shell) and a Host Control screen that shows the `link` command and lists and forgets linked computers.
  - Because the listener now runs from boot, anyone on the LAN can upload a Deck App or add a link whenever VitaDeck runs, until credentials exist (ADR 0004).
- **Demo:** `js/examples/host-control` lists every linked computer with live CPU, and for the selected one shows its capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip.

**Deviations from the issues:**
- The commands are plugins rather than a flat catalogue, so the wire request gains a `plugin` field.
- VitaDeck keeps several links, so the getter returns a JSON array, and the link payload carries a companion `id`.
- It ships as one PR instead of three, as asked; the commits still follow the slices.
- #111 has the Vita listen for links only while the Host Control screen is open. After testing, setup felt clunky, so links share the always-on LAN Listener with Runtime Upload.

ADR 0004, `CONTEXT.md` (new terms include **Host Control Plugin**, **Host Plugin Package** and **LAN Listener**), AGENTS.md and the READMEs are rewritten in place. Agent skills:
- New public `vitadeck-host-control`: companion, linking, plugin authoring and install, error codes.
- `vitadeck-deck-app-init`: learns `--host-plugin` and `--host-plugin-only`.
- `vitadeck-manual-testing`: gains a Host Control section.
- `vitadeck-vdapp-upload` and `vitadeck-build`: say where `.vdplugin.zip` goes and that `pnpm build` now builds the companion. Credentials are still deferred, so only read-only built-ins exist.

## Proof

- `scripts/agent-check.sh full` passed on 2a18bdfe (the head adds a JS-only review fix; fast tier passed on it): SDK tests 40/40, companion tests 37/37, lint and format, non-smoke CTest 18/18 including `host_control_link_harness`, the fetch-cancel case and the Shell's empty-library focus, Docker Linux smoke 2/2, and the Vita VPK build.
- New tests:
  - The SDK client, the companion and the C harness all replay the same contract fixtures in `tests/fixtures/host-control/`.
  - SDK CLI scaffolds:
    - `create --host-plugin`: typechecks, builds the package and zip, and its `greet` runs.
    - `create --host-plugin-only`: builds alone, and a separate Deck App imports its registry, typechecks and builds.
  - SDK CLI build:
    - `hostPlugin.files` is copied into the package.
    - A broken plugin build keeps the last good package.
    - Config and `dev` URL rules are enforced.
  - Companion CLI, end to end: zip `install` and `remove` against a running companion, `--plugin` folder reload, and a broken rebuild keeping the previous plugin.
  - Companion loader: rejects bad manifests and zips with several roots or `../` paths. A bundled CommonJS dependency and a package reading its own `files/` both work.
  - Events:
    - A held wait answers in under 1 s when the plugin emits, ignores other plugins, and starts over after a restart.
    - Stopped lifecycles' emits are dropped, an unloaded plugin answers `unknown_plugin`, `close` answers waits, and lifecycles start only after the port is bound.
    - CLI `notify` reaches a waiting `core.events`. `watchHostEvents` passes `next` as `after` and stops at once from a callback.
  - Native: `js_limits_harness` stops a Deck App while its fetch waits on a server that never answers. That took 15 s before the cancel fix and is under 3 s after.
- Manual passes in the macOS host window:
  - **Link and demo** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-control-screenshots/)): two companions linked, the demo's gauges and Echo, an offline companion, and forgetting a link.
  - **External user, from packed tarballs, with a globally installed companion** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-plugin-screenshots/)):
    - A `--host-plugin` app called its plugin, which read text from its packaged `files/`.
    - Editing a file and rebuilding reloaded live with no restart, and `remove` showed `unknown_plugin`.
    - A separate `deck` app depending on a standalone `lights` plugin (`npm install ../lights`) called it after `install lights.vdplugin.zip`.
    - `notify` showed in the demo within 0.4 s. The held `core.events` request had waited 12.6 s and answered in the same millisecond as `core.notify`; idle waits cycled at 25 s.

  - **LAN Listener** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/lan-listener-screenshots/)): with the Shell never opened, port 8787 was bound at startup, `link` and a `curl` upload both succeeded, and the demo showed the linked Mac. Turning **Upload and link** off made an upload fail with connection refused; turning it on restored it.

  - **Relink**: the companion started on a new port while VitaDeck was off, logged a retry, and relinked within 30 s of VitaDeck starting; the demo then polled the new port and refreshed its capabilities. After forgetting the computer in the Shell, a companion restart logged "forgot this computer", emptied its `vitas`, and the Vita stayed unlinked.
